title: Developmental physiology is the control layer between genotype and phenotype

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Developmental physiology is the control layer between genotype and phenotype

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors hold that biological genotypes do not code directly for phenotypes; developmental physiology, built from cells with their own context-sensitive behaviours, is the control layer separating genomes from the capacities that selection evaluates.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Biological genotypes do not code directly for phenotypes; developmental physiology is the control layer that separates genomes from capacities ascertained by selection.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “Abstract”. Scope: Multicellular organisms generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-competency-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim can be operationalized as added predictive and causal mediation by developmental state. Existing datasets cover restricted systems, not multicellular organisms generally.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across organisms and perturbations, model phenotype from genotype alone versus genotype plus measured developmental physiological states and compare out-of-sample prediction. A consistent added predictive and causal contribution from physiology supports the control-layer claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Control layer' is broad and partly metaphorical.

Few datasets jointly measure genotype, longitudinal physiology, and mature phenotype across perturbations.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public genetic-association data can document that genotypes do not map cleanly onto phenotypes, which is the empirical core of the negative clause. They do not measure developmental physiology as a control layer between genomes and selection. The framework claim is only partly pinned to existing data, and rival wordings fit the same catalogues.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether identical or near-identical genotypes yield systematically different phenotypes under documented developmental conditions, using variant-to-trait catalogues and regeneration or polyphenism studies. Widespread genotype–phenotype non-isomorphism would support the negative half; a direct, one-to-one encoding across developmental contexts would refute it. Calling developmental physiology the control layer remains a further interpretation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
GWAS misses developmental dynamics, so it cannot show that physiology is the layer selection evaluates.

Several evo-devo descriptions fit the same genotype–phenotype gaps.

fields.label: Dimension scores
